title: torilis helvetica subsp. purpurea
intro: Torilis helvetica subsp. purpurea, commonly known as Purple Hedge Parsley or Wild Chervil, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the carrot family (Apiaceae) that grows in various regions of Europe. The plant is used for its medicinal properties, which include its ability to aid digestion, reduce inflammation, and alleviate respiratory issues. The therapeutic actions of Torilis helvetica subsp. purpurea are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including sesquiterpenes, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. The plant's health benefits are also attributed to its ability to support the immune system, reduce oxidative stress, and exhibit hepatoprotective properties.
